thread:
incident-bot: HIGH: Traffic anomaly — rapid spike to /v1/batch endpoints from ~12.34.56.0/22 and several other ASN ranges. Error 429 increasing, latency ~2.8s p95. Auto-throttle triggered. Paging oncall.

maria (oncall): On it. picking this up — looking at dashboard now. pinging chris and omar.

chris (eng-sre): I see a huge number of small requests with identical user-agent: \"curl/7.82.0\" hitting /v1/batch with empty API token header. Rate per sec ~18k from those ranges.

omar (security): Likely scraper farm. Could be credential-less probing. Any successful auths?

maria (oncall): Checking auth logs — successful requests to customers are low. Most are 401/403 then 429 from our rate limiter. Looks like unauthenticated spam plus a few hit tokens that belong to non-prod.

chris (eng-sre): Quick mitigation plan: 1) Apply temporary WAF block for the top offending /24s. 2) Raise global per-IP token rate limiting from 120r/m -> 30r/m. 3) Disable unauthenticated batch endpoints temporarily (feature flag). 4) Notify support/account teams. Any objections?

omar (security): +1 on WAF blocks and lowering per-IP. Also suggest add challenge (CAPTCHA) for newly seen IP ranges hitting auth endpoints.

kevin (support): Heads-up — I'll prepare a short customer-facing blurb. Which customers will see impact?

maria (oncall): Initial check: about 23 customers are seeing 429s in the last 5m; most are high-volume test tenants. No enterprise paid customers flagged yet, but we'll run the account lookup.

samir (devex): If we disable unauthenticated batch it might affect some demo apps. Please list impacted routes so we can patch docs.

incident-bot: Action log: created incident INC-2026-184100, severity: high, pager: maria (oncall).

chris (eng-sre): Executing WAF rule now — adding IP ranges: 12.34.56.0/24, 12.34.58.0/24, 45.12.0.0/16. Rule: block with 403 for requests matching path:/v1/batch and UA containing \"curl\".

# Command run:
# wafctl add-block --ips 12.34.56.0/24,12.34.58.0/24,45.12.0.0/16 --match 'path:/v1/batch AND user_agent:curl' --reason "scraper spike 184100"

chris (eng-sre): WAF rule in place — seeing immediate drop from those ranges.

maria (oncall): Applying per-IP rate limit change now. Patch in feature flags to lower per-ip -> 30r/m for all batch endpoints.

# config snippet:
# "rate_limits": { "per_ip": { "v1/batch": "30/min" } }

maria (oncall): Rate limiter updated. p95 latency dropping to 0.9s, overall request rate dropped 60%. Some legitimate customers hitting the limit — seeing 429s from our own test accounts.

kevin (support): Noted. I'll DM the top 5 affected accounts and post a heads-up to #support. Draft: "We're seeing high traffic; we've applied protective rate limits on batch endpoints which may cause 429s. We're working on targeted relax for verified customers." Want me to post?

maria (oncall): Post it. Also list mitigation to whitelist verified enterprise IPs once we confirm.

omar (security): Recommend temporary token-only enforcement: reject requests without an API key to batch endpoints — can be toggled fast. That will cut unauthenticated load.

chris (eng-sre): Implementing token-only mode for /v1/batch (feature flag).

# config change:
# "auth_required": { "/v1/batch": true }

chris (eng-sre): Token-only mode rolled. Unauthenticated load dropped ~85%. Some degraded customers still seeing 429 because they use shared proxies.

samir (devex): For customers using demo accounts with no token, we'll need an opt-in dev mode. Keep me in the loop.

maria (oncall): Omar — can you look at source ASNs and see if there's reuse across regions? Might help if we do geo-throttle.

omar (security): Looking... big hits from ASNs in Eastern Europe and a known botnet ASN. I'm recommending geo-throttle on those countries for non-authenticated requests.

chris (eng-sre): Added geo-throttle: drop rate to 5r/m for country codes RU, BY, UA for /v1/batch unless token present.

maria (oncall): We're trending back to normal. p95 latency 0.6s, error budget holding.

kevin (support): Posted to #support and emailed affected customers. Two replies: one customer asked for ETA to restore normal throughput; one acknowledged and asked for a whitelist.

maria (oncall): Decision: Keep WAF blocks + per-ip limits + token-only enforcement for next 30m. Support will collect whitelist requests; we'll evaluate and add enterprise IPs to allowlist. If we see recovery, ramp down in 30m.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-184100 updated: mitigations applied: WAF block, per-ip rate limit reduced, token-only batch endpoints, geo-throttle.

chris (eng-sre): FYI disabled the batch streaming feature flag for unauthenticated clients (was getting abused to open long-lived sessions).

samir (devex): Noted. I'll update docs and the quickstart to emphasize token requirement for batch.

maria (oncall): Oncall handoff in 25m to chris (overnight). chris, I'll leave playbook: 1) Monitor p95 and 429 rate. 2) If legitimate customers get 429 > threshold (5 customers for >5m), rollback per-ip to 60r/m and open a targeted allowlist. 3) If traffic resurges, escalate to infra lead.

chris (eng-sre): Ack. I'll take the handoff.

omar (security): After-action items: collect full IP list, submit to abuse feeds, consider permanent WAF signature.

kevin (support): I'll compile affected customer list and send account contacts to chris for allowlist requests.

maria (oncall): Summary: mitigations reduced load ~85%, customer impact limited to non-enterprise/test tenants and a handful of customers who got 429s. No data exfil or successful credential stuffing observed. Moving to monitoring mode.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-184100 severity moved to \"monitoring\". Next update scheduled in 30m.

chris (eng-sre): Handoff complete. Leaving rule set enabled. Will escalate if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
